title: Elodie and the Hollow
premise: August Okonkwo has survived seven years in the city of Vell by carving bones into harmless trinkets, hiding the fact that he can hear the dead whisper through them. When a mute child named Elodie arrives at his door speaking the First Tongue—the language of the Hollow, the realm beneath the world—August learns she is the last living anchor of an ancient covenant that once kept both realms in balance. The city's witch-hunters, led by August's former mentor Seraphine Voss, hunt Elodie to sever the covenant permanently and end magic forever. As the moon nears its thirteenth turn, August must choose between loyalty to the mentor who saved his life and the truth that her crusade will unravel reality itself. In the end, August sacrifices his own hearing of the dead to reforge the covenant with Elodie as its new voice, banishing the Hollow's hunger while leaving him ordinary—and finally free.
about_author: Vesper Halloran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funerary carvings before turning to fiction. They write quiet, bone-deep fantasy about people who hear what others cannot.

chapters.title: The Quiet Trade
chapters.summary: POV: August. In the market city of Vell, August sells bone charms stripped of real power, trading small comforts for invisibility under the Edict Against Magic. He hears the dead murmur through his carvings but pretends not to. The beat: weary self-containment, a man who has made silence his craft.

chapters.title: A Knock Before Dawn
chapters.summary: POV: August. A mud-streaked girl appears at his door during a curfew storm, speaking words no living mouth should know—words his carved bones answer. She carries a shard of white antler that hums like a struck bell. The beat: dread and reluctant wonder; his hiding place is breached.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: POV: August. August tests Elodie's language against his oldest carvings and realizes she speaks the First Tongue of the Hollow, the realm below. The dead in his bones grow agitated, warning of a thirteenth moon. The beat: denial cracking into terrible recognition.

chapters.title: The Edict's Long Shadow
chapters.summary: POV: August. Flashback woven through present: seven years ago, Seraphine Voss spared young August from the purges on condition he abandon magic entirely. Now posters appear offering reward for a 'tongued child.' The beat: guilt over the debt that binds him to his hunter.

chapters.title: Elodie
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Through fragments and drawings, we learn Elodie escaped the Hollow's edge where her village 'sank quiet.' She cannot speak any tongue but the First, and the antler shard shows her visions of a broken door. The beat: loneliness meeting tentative trust.

chapters.title: The Bone-Carver's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV: August. August agrees to shelter Elodie until the moon turns, telling himself it's temporary. He begins carving a translation charm so they can communicate. The dead warn: 'the covenant starves.' The beat: cautious commitment disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Seraphine
chapters.summary: POV: Seraphine Voss. The witch-hunter commander interrogates a smuggler about the child, revealing her conviction that the Hollow murdered her family decades ago. She suspects a bone-carver who was once her student. The beat: righteous grief hardening into obsession.

chapters.title: The Market of Whispers
chapters.summary: POV: August. Seeking supplies, August visits an underground market of hidden practitioners and learns the covenant's history: thirteen moons ago it began failing, and each full moon since, something in the Hollow has grown hungrier. The beat: the stakes widen beyond one child.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn Rising
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Elodie's visions sharpen—she sees the Hollow's door held shut by thirteen anchors, twelve already dark. She draws August's face among the anchors without understanding why. The beat: fear becoming purpose; she may be meant to be sacrificed.

chapters.title: Old Debt, New Blade
chapters.summary: POV: Seraphine. Seraphine raids the underground market and finds traces of August's charm-work. Her lieutenant urges mercy; she refuses, believing mercy is how the Hollow spreads. The beat: the hunter closes in, still human, still wounded.

chapters.title: The Language Beneath
chapters.summary: POV: August. The translation charm works at last, and Elodie tells her story fully: she was chosen by the Hollow's dying wardens to carry the final anchor-word. August realizes reforging the covenant requires a speaker willing to give up their own voice's gift. The beat: the true cost comes into focus.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: POV: August. Seraphine arrives at August's door—not with soldiers, but alone, asking him to hand over the child as repayment for sparing his life. August stalls, torn between the woman who saved him and the truth he now knows. The beat: loyalty and truth collide head-on.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Salt Flats
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. August flees with Elodie toward the Hollow's edge, pursued by Seraphine's hunters. Crossing the salt flats, Elodie uses the First Tongue to calm a hunting beast, revealing the language can mend as well as bind. The beat: fugitive terror tempered by growing courage.

chapters.title: The Village That Sank Quiet
chapters.summary: POV: August. They reach Elodie's ruined village, half-swallowed by the Hollow's grey tide. Among the sunken houses, the dead speak clearly for the first time: the wardens did not die—they were consumed when the covenant weakened. The beat: grief and horror deepening resolve.

chapters.title: Seraphine's Truth
chapters.summary: POV: Seraphine. Following their trail, Seraphine finds evidence contradicting her life's mission: her family was killed not by the Hollow but by the first purge's zealots, who blamed the realm below. The beat: her certainty fractures; she rides on anyway, unable to stop.

chapters.title: The Door Below
chapters.summary: POV: August. At the threshold of the Hollow, August and Elodie find the great door cracked, hunger leaking through like cold smoke. Twelve anchor-stones stand dark. The dead offer August a choice: reforge the covenant and lose forever the voices that have been his only companionship. The beat: sacrifice named aloud.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Threshold
chapters.summary: POV: Seraphine. Seraphine's company corners them at the door. In the confrontation, Elodie speaks the First Tongue openly, and the Hollow's hunger responds—showing every hunter the truth of what its destruction would unleash. The beat: chaos, awe, and Seraphine standing at the edge of belief.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Anchor
chapters.summary: POV: August. With the moon at its zenith, August begins the reforging, carving the covenant into his own bones while Elodie lends her voice. Seraphine must choose: fire her crossbow or lower it. The beat: the climax—loyalty transmuted into truth at last.

chapters.title: Silence Given Freely
chapters.summary: POV: August. August completes the covenant, pouring his gift of hearing into the anchor-stones. The dead's voices fade one by one, each farewell a small heartbreak, until only Elodie's voice remains, speaking gratitude in words he can no longer hear but somehow understands. The beat: sorrow braided with peace.

chapters.title: After the Turning
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. The Hollow settles into balance; the grey tide recedes from the village. Elodie, now able to learn ordinary speech, chooses to stay near August rather than return to what remains of her old life. The beat: two orphans of different silences finding belonging together.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's New Trade
chapters.summary: POV: August. Months later, August carves again—but now purely for beauty, no whispers inside. Seraphine, resigned from the hunt, visits with bread and an awkward apology neither fully needs. The Edict stands, but enforcement has quietly softened. The beat: earned quiet, imperfect forgiveness.

chapters.title: Elodie and the Hollow
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. On the first anniversary of the thirteenth turn, Elodie teaches August the shapes of First Tongue words he'll never hear, writing them in salt on his workbench. Beneath the floor, faint and contented, something ancient turns over in its sleep. The beat: belonging without possession—an ending that hums.
